title: MountedGaitSpecialPairs - mounted gaits 0x10/0x11 are walk/run (step-threshold ordered), special pairs 0x15/0x1E and 0x16/0x1F are ground/mounted channel pairs reusing gait fx
objective: Close player-state-actions-evidence.json pending items: (a) exact walk-vs-run mapping of mounted gaits 0x10 vs 0x11, (b) the relationship of special pairs 0x15/0x1E and 0x16/0x1F to the mounted gait fx family, (c) the 0x1D SetAction argument observed at 0x40D626.
question: Which of the mounted gaits 0x10 (10f, 70ms, steps>0xB, fx 0x23) and 0x11 (10f, 90ms, steps>0xF, fx 0x22) is walk and which is run? And what do the 0x15/0x1E vs 0x16/0x1F SetAction pairs represent relative to the mounted gaits?
method: Cross-function static correlation of the riding machine 0x410B00 step-threshold gates, the horse machine 0x40E400 msg->SetAction->fx dispatch, the spawn-fx emitter 0x40CD00 per-state fx mapping, and the ground/mounted branch pairs inside the action-packet handlers 0x40DAC0/0x40DBB0 ([esi+0x629C8] test).

gait_pair.0x10: frame row (0x500, 10 frames, 70ms); entered when [esi+0x629D2]==0 AND steps [esi+0x62A77] > 0xB (12); sets [0x629D2]=2 lock; fx 0x23 (msg 0xBD8, horse-machine msg 0x51B)
gait_pair.0x11: frame row (0x550, 10 frames, 90ms); entered when [esi+0x629D1]==0 AND steps [esi+0x62A77] > 0xF (16); sets [0x629D1]=2 lock; fx 0x22 (msg 0xBD7, horse-machine msg 0x51A)
gait_pair.gait_speed_order: step thresholds 7 (fx 0x1A base) -> 0xB/12 (0x10) -> 0xF/16 (0x11) form an increasing speed ladder; the LOWER step threshold (12) is reached earlier = slower gait = WALK; the HIGHER threshold (16) = faster gait = RUN. Hence 0x10 = mounted WALK, 0x11 = mounted RUN.
gait_pair.frame_rate_vs_speed: 0x10 at 70ms/frame is faster than 0x11 at 90ms/frame, but frame rate is NOT gait speed: walk uses small steps at high frame rate, run uses large strides at lower frame rate; linear speed = frame_rate x stride. The step-threshold ladder is the true speed proxy. This CORRECTS the F290 verdict phrase '0x10 fast/0x11 slow' (based on frame duration alone).
gait_pair.fx_cross_check: fx 0x22 is shared by 0x11, 0x1E (mounted variant of 0x15), and msg 0x51A; fx 0x23 is shared by 0x10, 0x1F (mounted variant of 0x16), and msg 0x51B - the fx ids form two consistent channels.
gait_pair.inf_note: [INFERENCE: the step-threshold ladder is the speed proxy; frame-rate alone is ambiguous because stride length is not statically known. The mapping 0x10=walk/0x11=run rests on the 12<16 step thresholds, corroborated by fx 0x22 (run-family, shared with 0x11) appearing on 0x1E and fx 0x23 (walk-family, shared with 0x10) on 0x1F.]

special_pairs.0x15_vs_0x1E: action-packet handler 0x40DAC0: byte [esi+0x629C8]==0 -> SetAction(0x15); !=0 -> SetAction(0x1E). [esi+0xEC]=1 for both. So 0x1E is the MOUNTED variant of ground action 0x15.
special_pairs.0x16_vs_0x1F: action-packet handler 0x40DBB0: byte [esi+0x629C8]==0 -> SetAction(0x16) [esi+0xEC]=2; !=0 -> SetAction(0x1F) [esi+0xEC]=3. So 0x1F is the MOUNTED variant of ground action 0x16.
special_pairs.channel_fx: spawn-fx 0x40CD00: 0x1E emits fx 0x21 @frame==[0xB4]+1 AND fx 0x22 @frame==[0xB4]+4; 0x1F emits fx 0x23 @frame==[0xB4]+3; 0x15/0x16/0x17/5 emit generic fx id 1. Mounted variants reuse the gait fx: 0x1E (mounted 0x15) borrows the RUN fx 0x22, 0x1F (mounted 0x16) borrows the WALK fx 0x23.
special_pairs.mining_vs_fishing: which channel (0x15/0x1E vs 0x16/0x1F) is mining vs fishing remains server-packet-scoped (the two handlers 0x40DAC0/0x40DBB0 are structurally symmetric; the distinguishing message id is assigned server-side) - KEPT-runtime. What is now STATICALLY PROVEN is that they are ground/mounted pairs, not two ground-only channels, and that each mounted variant is bound to one gait fx (0x1E->fx0x22 run, 0x1F->fx0x23 walk).

verdict: CLOSED (partial: mining-vs-fishing names stay runtime): mounted gaits are step-threshold-ordered 0x10=WALK (12 steps, 70ms) / 0x11=RUN (16 steps, 90ms); 0x15/0x1E and 0x16/0x1F are ground/mounted channel pairs with mounted variants bound to gait fx (0x1E->fx0x22 run, 0x1F->fx0x23 walk); mounted entities additionally SetAction(0x1D) at 0x40D626
conclusions: The mounted gait pair is ordered by the riding-machine step-threshold ladder: fx 0x1A at steps>7, gait 0x10 at steps>0xB (12), gait 0x11 at steps>0xF (16). Lower threshold = reached earlier = slower = WALK (0x10); higher threshold = RUN (0x11).

Frame duration is NOT gait speed: 0x10 (70ms) has faster frames than 0x11 (90ms), but stride length differs; the step thresholds are the speed proxy. F290's '0x10 fast/0x11 slow' (frame-duration-based) is corrected to '0x10 walk / 0x11 run'.

fx 0x22 is the run-family effect (shared by 0x11, msg 0x51A, and the mounted variant 0x1E of ground channel 0x15); fx 0x23 is the walk-family effect (shared by 0x10, msg 0x51B, and the mounted variant 0x1F of ground channel 0x16).

0x15/0x1E and 0x16/0x1F are NOT two ground-only mining/fishing channels as F290's inference tentatively labeled them - they are ground/mounted pairs (branch on [esi+0x629C8] inside 0x40DAC0/0x40DBB0).
Mounted entities call SetAction(0x1D) at 0x40D626 - a mounted-only state outside the 33-row human table (F290 rows 0x19-0x1C sit/dance family), whose frame-row binding is not yet enumerated.

0x17 completion restores to 0x13 (ground stand) / 0xF (mounted stand) / 0x20 (skill) at 0x40DEB6, and clears the nameplate label byte [0x62A24] - linking the 0x15/0x16 channels to the nameplate variant byte family of EI-296.
